The search for a counterpart in 2023 did not identify a disclosure with the same specific subject matter. Candidate intc_2023_1A_D043 focuses on customer concentration risk (top 3 customers), while intc_2023_1A_D041 focuses on distributor/channel partner risks. Neither describes the general business-to-business sales structure and customer base definition in the same manner. Thus, no direct match found.

The 2025 filing discusses risks related to the foundry business strategy (D003) and customer concentration (D035), but does not contain a general risk disclosure describing the scope of Intel's customer base and sales channels (OEMs, ODMs, cloud providers, resellers) as a primary risk factor in the same manner as the 2024 disclosure. The closest related risk is D034 (distribution risks) or D035 (customer concentration), but neither captures the general business model description of D048.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates (amd_2024_1A_D014, amd_2024_1A_D066) focus exclusively on risks related to Microsoft and software vendor support for operating systems and applications. Intel's disclosure concerns its global distribution network and customer base composition (OEMs, ODMs, cloud providers). There is no substantive overlap in the specific topic of distribution channels or customer base mechanics between Intel's text and AMD's software dependency risks.

The retrieved candidates (avgo_2024_1A_D060, avgo_2024_1A_D065) address software business growth, hybrid-cloud shifts, and product lifecycle management. These topics are distinct from Intel's disclosure regarding its global hardware distribution channels and primary customer types (OEMs, ODMs). No candidate discusses Intel's specific channel model or customer base composition.

The retrieved candidates (mu_2024_1A_D034, mu_2024_1A_D012) focus on system-level solution development, manufacturing costs, and product specification failures. While these involve customer specifications, they do not address the global distribution channels or the specific mix of OEM/ODM/cloud customer bases that characterize Intel's disclosure. The topics are operationally distinct (manufacturing/process risk vs. channel/customer base risk).

comparisons.peer_topic: Indirect sales channel impact on demand forecasting
comparisons.peer_summary: End customers often purchase indirectly through OEMs, ODMs, and distributors, whose decisions and downstream estimates impact the company's ability to properly forecast demand.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA disclose risks associated with indirect sales channels involving OEMs and ODMs. Intel describes its primary sales to OEMs, ODMs, and cloud service providers who incorporate its solutions into end products. Similarly, NVIDIA highlights that many end customers purchase indirectly through OEMs, ODMs, system integrators, and distributors. The key difference is that NVIDIA explicitly links this channel structure to demand forecasting challenges and reliance on downstream estimates, whereas Intel focuses on describing the customer base and channel composition without explicitly citing forecasting difficulty as a risk in this specific disclosure.

sentences.text: We sell our products primarily to OEMs, ODMs, and cloud service providers.

In addition, our customers include other manufacturers and service providers, such as industrial and communication equipment manufacturers and cloud service providers who buy our products through distributor, reseller, retail, and OEM channels throughout the world.
Many end customers often do not purchase directly from us but instead purchase indirectly through multiple OEMs, ODMs, system integrators, distributors, and other channel partners.

As a result, the decisions made by our multiple OEMs, ODMs, system integrators, distributors, and other channel partners, and in response to changing market conditions and changes in end-user demand for our products, have impacted and could in the future continue to impact our ability to properly forecast demand, particularly as they are based on estimates provided by various downstream parties.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates (qcom_2024_1A_D092, qcom_2024_1A_D002) focus on the cyclical nature of the semiconductor industry and device share concentration among specific OEMs (particularly Chinese OEMs). While Qualcomm mentions OEMs, the context is revenue concentration and industry volatility, whereas Intel's disclosure defines its primary sales channels (OEMs, ODMs, cloud providers) as part of its business model description without discussing revenue concentration risks or industry cyclicality in this specific segment.
